translations: The slight misalignment relaxed the tension for a moment, but it didn't turn the adult's footprint into a laughingstock. Hu Xue asked everyone to step back to the edge and look for adjacent marks. On the other side of Shallow Island, there was indeed a fainter indentation, consistent in direction, like the footprint of a towering being who had passed through the Thunder Sea.

She observed the water's surface in the indentation. Outside, the wind was constantly blowing, but the water in the indentation was calmer; when a distant thunderclap sounded, fine lines would appear spreading out from the center. The direction of the footprint was towards the center of the sea, and the edge of the mud didn't show any recent collapse, indicating that the giant footprint had been there for a long time, but hadn't been completely washed away by the rainwater.

Hu Xue left a normal person's footprint next to it. When the rainwater flowed through, the small footprint's edges quickly dispersed, but the giant footprint's edges remained like they had been pressed into a deeper layer of soil, maintaining their shape. The comparison ruled out the guess that someone had dug a hole to play a trick, and it also calmed down the people who were originally competing to find the treasure.

She asked her companions to recount what they had seen separately. Some people only remembered "big," some only remembered the thunder, until Hu Xue asked them to recall the toe marks, direction, and adjacent marks, and they finally realized that the strange phenomenon required an accurate observation, and couldn't be replaced by a single phrase "scary."

Someone wanted to measure the footprint with a rope. As soon as one end of the rope was placed down, a thunderclap suddenly sounded, and the group quickly retreated to a safe place. Aman was collecting the bamboo slips when the wind blew a few pages loose, and he tightly hugged them, whispering, "The north wind of the North Sea once wanted to see my records, and this Thunder Sea is also very enthusiastic."

Hu Xue told him to shut up and protect the bamboo slips. The thunderstorm came quickly, but only lasted for a short time. When they returned to Shallow Island, the normal animal tracks had been washed away, but the adult footprint still maintained its shape, and the water had become even clearer.

The group confirmed that they were indeed looking at an intact adult footprint. There was no thunder god appearing to fight monsters, and no one brought an explanation. The mystery was within the footprint itself: what kind of existence had left such a footprint, and why did the thunder and the ripples in the water match?

Hu Xue decided to wait until the thunderstorm had completely subsided before approaching the footprint alone. She wouldn't let anyone jump into the water to test their luck, but only stood at a safe distance to observe the water and the thunder. The adult footprint was in the center of Shallow Island; whether to enter it, she would have to choose herself, balancing her fear and clarity of mind.
By the afternoon, the thunderclouds moved away.

The water in the adult footprint began to recede, revealing fine mud lines at the bottom. Hu Xue stood at the edge, and could clearly see the toe marks and the center of the footprint. Her companions advised her to only observe from the outside, because no one knew what would happen if she entered.

Hu Xue didn't know either. That's why she didn't let anyone rush in out of curiosity, and she didn't say that the unknown was a certain good omen. She asked everyone to retreat to a high place, and if the thunderclouds reformed, they would immediately leave; she took off her basket and kept only a long probe.

She first touched the bottom of the footprint with the probe. The mud was solid, without any deep holes. The water's residual light danced with the probe's shadow, but the distant thunder didn't change. If the adult footprint was just a giant old mark, entering it might not lead to anything; if it was connected to the Thunder Sea's mysterious phenomenon, this step would bring the unknown to her.

Hu Xue walked around to the front of the footprint, where it pointed, and saw that the next faint mark had disappeared into the water. That direction didn't seem to lead people back to the shore, but rather towards the deeper part of the Thunder Sea. She therefore didn't let the group advance collectively, but only reconfirmed her own observations and escape route.

Hu Xue thought of the missing herbs among her people, and the observations she had made along the way. People couldn't forever rely on rumors to understand the world, but personally exploring it didn't mean being reckless. She placed the probe outside the footprint, lifted one foot, and stepped into it along the direction of the giant footprint's center.

Her foot landed on the mud lines, and the footprint was still large enough to contain a wide area around it. She didn't fall, didn't sink, and no ambiguous shadow appeared. The first change was in the water in the footprint: the light from her foot spread out in layers along the arch of her foot and the direction of her toes.

Immediately after, a long thunderclap sounded from the deeper part of the Thunder Sea. The sound wasn't like a nearby thunderclap, but rather like the earth and the water responding together. The reeds bent down, water birds flew up from the distant island, and a beam of light fell on the adult footprint.
